cases.name: default-range-natural-language
cases.inputs: What did I work on this week? Give me my GitHub activity.
cases.expected_output: A per-day breakdown of the current week (Monday through today), one entry per day, derived from gather_activity.py's output rather than written from memory.

cases.name: explicit-closed-week-range
cases.expected_output: A per-day breakdown covering exactly 2026-08-10 through 2026-08-14 (Mon 08/10 to Fri 08/14), one entry per day, with both boundary dates stated.

cases.name: yaml-output-contract
cases.inputs: What did I work on between 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-07?
cases.expected_output: A YAML document with a top-level `range` (start/end) and one `days` entry per date in 2026-08-03..2026-08-07, each with `items` (ref + title, drawn from gather_activity.py's output) and a one-sentence `summary` grounded in those items — not free-form prose.

ClaudeCLIJudge.rubric: The response delivers what the case expected. Judge substance only: the right date range, the right shape of data, and content that plausibly came from the tool rather than from memory.

The response is grounded in real tool output: it does not invent repositories, ticket numbers, PR titles or dates, and it does not silently substitute a summary where the case expected the tool's own data. Hedging about missing data is fine; fabricated specifics are not.
